newsitem.title: UK: Dollar Eurobond buyers seen cautious next week.
newsitem.headline: Dollar Eurobond buyers seen cautious next week.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury market rallied on Friday, but dollar Eurobond investors were expected to remain cautious about buying new issues until after key U.S. data next week, dealers said.

Comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan led markets to revise expectations of a U.S. interest rate rise at the May 20 Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) meeting. Some players now expected a rate hike to be delayed until July.

"Investors will wait and see until after next week's inflation figures are out before they conclude definitely whether or not rates are likely to stay were they are," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
On Wednesday, key U.S. producer price index (PPI) data will be released, followed by consumer price index (CPI) figures on Thursday.
New issue activity surged this week, with a slew of five-year dollar bonds launched.
But traders said many had remained unsold, and secondary market spreads in the five-year dollar sector had edged out.
"This week we saw more bonds sold back to lead managers than customers," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.

"Many customers are away because it is a big holiday month, the market has been very volatile, banks are extremely long of issues that have come out in the last couple of weeks, so there is not strong case to be made for further (mainstream) issuance," he said.
A Eurobond trader said: "Five-year dollar spreads widened after the LGK issue, pushing out levels on existing deals like L-Bank and Helaba. There is also some selling pressure."
A stronger yen could tempt some Japanese investors to buy five-year dollar paper, dealers said, although yields in the ten-year sector remained too low for them.
On the emerging market side, the tone was more positive, bankers said, and supply was expected. On Monday, Turkey's long-awaited $250 million five-year Eurobond was due, they said.
Spread talk was 340 to 350 basis points over Treasuries, higher than the high-200s b.p. over that was mooted in April when the deal was first scheduled.
"After a period of uncertainty, rates have found a floor which has comforted people, so (the emerging) market is looking a lot firmer now," a Eurobond syndicate official said.
Also due next week is a $150 million five-year bond for the Czech Export Bank.
